parts.note: a brand is a kind or make of product

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word boy

explanation.surface: A good-natured lad ends up with something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, a common drink.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for dress is read from bottom to top

parts.note: garb is clothing, a synonym of dress

explanation.surface: Someone puts on smart clothes for a night of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Brag is an old British card game, an ancestor of poker.

definitions.meaning: the ... were a Germanic people who settled in early England
a point of view or perspective on something

explanation.surface: An early German person comes into sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were an early Germanic tribe, and a slant or perspective is a way of seeing things.

clue.text: Be a scared man, shaking, where skeletons rise from their graves

definitions.text: where skeletons rise from their graves

indicators.note: shaking signals that the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A frightened man trembles in a graveyard where skeletons come out to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The dance of death is an artistic theme, famously Saint-Saëns's piece, in which skeletons rise to dance.

clue.text: Strike-breaker classified as blackleg for starters?

definitions.text: Strike-breaker classified as blackleg for starters?

indicators.note: for starters asks for the opening letter of each of the four preceding words

explanation.surface: A strike-breaker is labelled a blackleg, the usual insult.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: it defines the answer and its first letters spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who breaks a strike is called a scab, also known in Britain as a blackleg.

definitions.meaning: someone who charges, billing a customer
a war horse ridden by a knight or cavalry officer

explanation.surface: Someone sends out a bill for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: One who charges is literally one invoicing, and a knight's war mount bears the same name.

definitions.meaning: a short rest or pause from work
a lung is something that breathes, playfully named by function

explanation.surface: A broken lung, a medical worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A short rest is a common informal term, and a lung is literally an organ that breathes.

indicators.note: around signals the letters of the word right are moved about

explanation.surface: A remark about something that encircles one's waist.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'around' jumbles RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Girth is the measurement round one's waist or middle.

clue.text: Mining, lesson one: the choice is yours!

definitions.meaning: the first lesson for a miner: get hold of your mattock-like tool
an invitation to choose whichever you like

explanation.surface: A mining instructor opens the first lesson by saying the choice is yours.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase invites someone to select freely, and literally tells a novice miner to grab a tool.

indicators.note: torn asunder means broken apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation is torn apart once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a South American country.

definitions.meaning: the card counted as one in each suit of a pack

explanation.surface: A specialist dressed in a business suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled person is called a crack or star, and the top card of each suit counts as one.

parts.note: old shellac records spun at this many revolutions per minute, and it is also a year, as in 1978

explanation.surface: A year when records were broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' suggests a best-ever achievement, but it is a gramophone disc named for its speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Old gramophone discs were called by their rpm speed, and the number also names a year.

indicators.note: in places the word for cut inside the word for branch

parts.note: a wing is a branch of a building or organisation
to hack is to cut roughly

explanation.surface: A massive cut is made in a tree limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacking is British informal for very large, as in a whacking great bill.

indicators.note: decapitates means the head, the first letter, is cut off the poet's name

parts.note: Walt Whitman, the American poet of Leaves of Grass

explanation.surface: A murderer beheads an American poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract killer is hired to murder someone.

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Eat long bananas and then some other fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like part of the fruit bowl but means crazy, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo, a fruit other than bananas.

indicators.note: did you say asks us to hear the word, not spell it

parts.note: a course is a direction taken

explanation.surface: A query about a vague set of directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means rough in texture or manner.

definitions.meaning: slang for a strong strain of cannabis

explanation.surface: Calling someone a weed and a nasty piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang both for potent cannabis and for a contemptible person, like the smelly animal.

clue.text: Cross river shortly behind two vessels

indicators.note: behind places the river after the two vessels

parts.note: a can (a container) and a tanker (a ship) are two kinds of vessel

indicators.note: shortly means the river's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Someone crosses a river shortly after two boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb about the river but is the adjective meaning grumpy. 'two vessels' supplies both CAN and TANKER. The Ouse is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantankerous person is bad-tempered, annoyed or irritable.

clue.text: One in common up for marriage

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole is read from bottom to top
in places the numeral inside the word for common

parts.note: non-U is British slang for not upper class, hence common
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone ordinary is offered for marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses NOINU, which is I put 'in' NON-U, the term for not upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining of two people in matrimony.

parts.note: on means in contact with, touching

indicators.note: borders asks for the outer letters of the word leafy

explanation.surface: Leafy hedges are just touching.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and merely both mean nothing more than.

clue.text: Frozen stuff featuring in Arctic expedition

indicators.note: featuring in means the letters appear inside the words Arctic expedition

explanation.surface: Frozen material on a polar journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water is the obvious stuff found in the Arctic.

indicators.note: edited means the letters of the preceding words are reworked

explanation.surface: An editor appears in an edited new version of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges EDITOR IN into RENDITIO, then N for 'new' finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a performance or interpretation of a piece, a version of it.

indicators.note: not entirely means the phrase is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to go off is to leave

explanation.surface: Was it an error to depart? Only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is informal for a silly blunder or error.

indicators.note: in places the word for bar inside the word for the air

parts.note: the sky is the air above us
an inn is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A thin bar hangs up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny means very thin, lean or slender.
